3e92ce18-fdf6-4a3a-a459-3bd013fd31cf.text_lemmatized: Mitosis has five phases: Interphase, Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, and Telophase.

936c1688-d882-46c3-b84f-e7c0cabbc872.data: During Interphase, the DNA in the cell is copied in preparation for cell division, resulting in two identical complete sets of chromosomes.
936c1688-d882-46c3-b84f-e7c0cabbc872.text_lemmatized: During Interphase, the DNA in the cell is copied in preparation for cell division, resulting in two identical complete sets of chromosomes.

0e0e0192-53ac-4a66-9c10-2da47f018f4d.data: In Prophase, chromosomes condense into X-shaped structures that can be easily seen under a microscope, with each chromosome composed of two sister chromatids containing identical genetic information.
0e0e0192-53ac-4a66-9c10-2da47f018f4d.text_lemmatized: In Prophase, chromosomes condense into X-shaped structures that can be easily seen under a microscope, with each chromosome composed of two sister chromatids containing identical genetic information.

c796e0b3-b019-466a-bb73-910a3758a77b.data: During Metaphase, chromosomes line up neatly end-to-end along the center (equator) of the cell, with the mitotic spindle fibers attaching to each of the sister chromatids.
c796e0b3-b019-466a-bb73-910a3758a77b.text_lemmatized: During Metaphase, chromosomes line up neatly end-to-end along the center (equator) of the cell, with the mitotic spindle fibers attaching to each of the sister chromatids.

326bed7e-444b-471a-b058-ea87fda89cba.data: In Anaphase, the sister chromatids are pulled apart by the mitotic spindle, with one chromatid being pulled to one pole and the other chromatid to the opposite pole.
326bed7e-444b-471a-b058-ea87fda89cba.text_lemmatized: In Anaphase, the sister chromatids are pulled apart by the mitotic spindle, with one chromatid being pulled to one pole and the other chromatid to the opposite pole.
